quest.title: Rowboat's Wake
quest.description: "Ever drifting down the stream, lingering in the golden gleam..."
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x250, Primogem x30, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x2

chapter.num: In the Wake of Narcissus: Act IV
chapter.title: Rowboat's Wake

talks.objective: Talk to Ann and re-seal the entrance to the Primordial Sea

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Yep, let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The entrance is sealed once more with the power of the Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text:
"I see."
The person who almost saved the world spoke: "The Holy Blade need not be a sword. It could even be a gold-haired outlander."
"And now the younger sister, who never stood forth as part of the adventure, has grasped a sword at last."

With that, you return to the Narzissenkreuz Ordo...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I knew you'd come back in one piece.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And we're glad that you and Seymour are okay!

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: In fact, the floor was quickly flooded by the rising water level, incapacitating the security machinery.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Mr. Caterpillar carried me out under his arm.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I said "in one piece," and indeed, everyone is accounted for. So, how is there one more person here?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Well, allow me to introduce Narzissenkreuz. Or, rather, what's left of Narzissenkreuz.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: ...Master.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: You've made progress, Caterpillar. You seem even more human now than you did centuries ago.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I thought I'd be more excited to see you... but I feel unexpectedly calm.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Over the last several hundred years, I've read many books and come to understand more about your teachings — as well as some of the absurdities in your theories.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Image record of the individual known as "Narzissenkreuz" has been updated. Please do not make any sudden moves, Narzissenkreuz.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Silly dog, you're not going to initiate your Mass Annihilation Mode again, are you?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: I judge that the threat he constitutes to you is low. Still, do not make any sudden moves, Narzissenkreuz.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: Ah, Alain Guillotin's creation. I once saw a bright future for it, that it could perhaps achieve what the ancient peoples' golems could not... Not that it matters now.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: Could you let me inspect its internals? Just out of a desire for knowledge, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Seymour's our companion, you know!

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: Fine.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: "Saving the world" is usually just poetic rhetoric one employs to alleviate mental illness...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Whether it takes the form of protecting the flame of a candle until the pilgrimage is done, or writing a story that allows fiction to invade reality.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Did you recover from your malady in the end?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Master, you now know what became of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo. What will you do next?

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: There may be a hint of irony in your voice when you call me "Master," but I will accept it nonetheless.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: You surely know about your birth?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I'm not interested in that anymore. You were simply toying with life — a kind of indifference I find despicable.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: I will accept that, too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Your attitude is so negative. Have you given up on yourself?

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: I will answer your question, then. My offer from before still stands. I will reveal the mysteries to them and answer any questions.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: In that case...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Please take Ann to find out the truth about her origins.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You explain the other Mary-Ann to Narzissenkreuz...

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: Ah, so that's what happened to the Director and Mary-Ann.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: I will help you, of course. It is something I ought to do.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: Let us go to the Kingdom Through the Looking-Glass together.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Well, as for your wish from before, Paimon, I've done everything I can. I'll be staying out of whatever happens next.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What wish?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Is your memory that much worse than mine? Didn't you ask me to help you help Ann and Seymour?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, right! But why don't you want to come with us, then?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I think the next matter is very personal for Ann and Mary-Ann. That scene doesn't call for a character like me.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: #But you, {NICKNAME} and Paimon, are different. You're the heroes of this story.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yes, the mighty heroine Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Well, Paimon should actually be...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Be what? Hm? You're not about to say something mean, are you, Caterpillar?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Whatever do you mean? You're the kind, guiding fairy at the hero's side, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... F—Fine! Paimon will take that!

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Once you finish up over there, let us things-that-used-to-be-human have a little reunion.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: #Should I go with {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, then?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Of course you should. I mean, you've been seeking the end of the quest this whole time. You, too, need an answer, don't you?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: I apologize. I do not understand.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: In that case, Seymour, you wait for us with Caterpillar.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: It's settled then. When it's just about time, I'll bring you to them.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Understood.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Seymour, Caterpillar... Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Shall we?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright! Let's go find Mary-Ann!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, this is even worse than last time... How's everything back to the way it was?

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: Ann, you of purest water — visualize in detail what this place would be like if all obstacles receded before you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Will that do anything?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Caterpillar said before that the story has already lost its meaning. As such, these imaginary things aren't necessary anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: This is how it might be for a low-level seeker. However, you are also the master of this place.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: Some believe the world to be only a prison of suffering, devoid of meaning. But you wield power over this place. So, rewrite it — imbue it with meaning.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: Only the hubris of one who believes themselves above the world can give rise to miracles.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: Had I not fervently believed I was above the apocalypse, I would not be where I am now.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Are you saying that you also believe the world has meaning?

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: Why else would I have made so many plans to save it?

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: On second thought, perhaps Caterpillar was right, and one only seeks the world's salvation to prove that they themselves deserve it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon doesn't really get what that means.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: Only by transforming oneself into a being of light to bring hope to a darkened world may one be permitted to enter the eternal kingdom of light after death.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: Are martyrs who perish for the world's sins undeserving of salvation?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon gets it... and doesn't get it at the same time.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: It is no matter. My teachings no longer have an audience.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: Oceanid Ann — can you do what I said?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I'll give it a try.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're amazing, Ann!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're amazing, Ann!

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Thank you. But I don't feel that amazing... Why is that?

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: Because this is something you would normally take for granted. You have simply remembered a fragment of your origin.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: Let us press on.

talks.objective: Dodge the cannon fire and break through the Bubble Formation

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Go back...

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Please, I beg of you...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mary-Ann's voice really is getting weaker. It's gone from a command to a request...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Still, it sure doesn't look like she's begging us!

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: Can you push yourself still further, Ann?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: It's fine. Since we've already come this far, there's no point in turning back now.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Forgive me, Mary-Ann, but we must get through this place.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You got rid of them all, Ann?

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: It's pointless to resist the truth. Ann merely denied that futile resistance.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: Let's keep moving forward.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The door here is shut! How are we going to get inside now...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, if we can't get in, then we can't get to that dizzying corridor and room, and can't jump down to that place where we fought Narcissus...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: No problem. Allow me to ensure this visit of ours won't be in vain.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Liddell is also nothing more than a figment of the Red Empress' dream. And this time, it's time to wake up.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: Indeed, that is the case.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: An explanation? What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: My operations require energy and commands, not explanations.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Still... Maintaining a primary directive system and logic module that both constantly return errors has brought me to the verge of shutdown.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Perhaps... I do... need some assistance.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Why... Why couldn't you just leave us here in peace?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mary-Ann!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We... We should be able to help you this time! Please, let us in!

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: No! I don't need your help! Please leave, I'm begging you...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Princess Lyris. Your story should have you living happily ever after. I won't give up.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: #This barrier is composed of an extremely hard and resistant will. But the Holy Blade is in your hands now, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If Paimon remembers correctly, the Holy Blade should be able to cut through any will that comes from water...

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: Correct, clever one.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I've got it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sorry, Mary-Ann. Just bear with us.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Don't come back here again. It's warm here, and I like it that way.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Don't come to me with your expectations — with that determined look on your face.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Just leave me alone, till the consciousness that keeps this form together fades away...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Perhaps I should have proposed a toast, "to us who were once human."

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Though, I don't think any of us could imbibe the way we are now.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: Was there anything that could not be said before we set off?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I'm just giving you a chance. It may not have been a good time for you to say some things back there.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: You could tell? Well, it cannot be helped.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: I have expended too much of my power. I shall not remain able to maintain myself for long.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: But... Why?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: We worked so hard to...

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: ... But before I disappear, tell me what you have learned over these last few centuries.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: I would like to know what sort of dreams you had.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: #Until I met Knight {NICKNAME} and Paimon... I was always searching for Princess Lyris.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Even after learning the truth — that I was just a character in someone's dream — I have no regrets.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: That's because I've already completed the best and greatest adventure of all. Perhaps my reward is being able to turn my dreams into reality.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I was just going back and forth between prison and books, occasionally dreaming about parts of my previous life.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: There were times when I wondered whether the butterfly became me, or I became the butterfly.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: But once I awoke, I would realize that I was only a caterpillar. The butterfly is also me, but whether it's the future or past me is hard to say.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: Dreams, magic, memories, esotericism.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: All that I once held dear now seems worthless to me.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: During the first ten years, I focused all my power on preventing the dissipation of my will.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: During the years that followed, I used that potent will to construct a universe within myself to resist my coming fate. That is how I held on.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: I suppose it is the same for you — to build a beautiful dream out of the ruins of what was once our home. That is an incredible thing.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: Mary-Ann was right. It's warm here.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Yes, I know.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: I grow weary. Ann, please leave me here.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: Farewell.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: He never did change his name back to Rene, did he?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: "Life, what is it but a dream?"...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Oh! So this is where the adventure we and Ann had came from.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No wonder everything was so chaotic. It wasn't finished!

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Yeah. I couldn't figure an ending out.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: At that point, everything had fallen apart. But the more such things happen, the more we want a simple, happy ending.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You know, sometimes you say "I" and sometimes you say "we"... Are you really Mary-Ann, or are you Lyris, the Oceanid they're always talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: I don't know... Well, not that it matters anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ann! Caterpillar! You're back!

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Where's Rene?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: He...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: ...He was a bit tired, so he went to rest.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmph! Well, Paimon hopes he turns over a new leaf and stops causing trouble!

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Seymour, you can come over now.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Understood.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Ms. Mary-Ann! Ms. Mary-Ann...

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: ...Your new hair and eye colors are simply dazzling.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Honestly, you silly dog. Is that all you can say?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: My language center is unable to express the information I am processing.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: I know. You're the same as ever...

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: ...Sorry. I missed you so much...

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: ...Right, so such things happened, huh? Then there's Jakob...

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: #{M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME} and Ms. Paimon's description largely fits with the facts. But one thing must be added.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: My power output during combat has been far below expectations. This is because over 30 percent of my components were damaged during the battle at Elynas and have not been maintained since.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: I hope you will consider this when evaluating my performance and will not choose to scrap me.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Of course not!

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: You have always been strong and brave. You are much more resilient than "we" are, Seymour.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Indeed. My designer, Alain Guillotin, is Fontaine's leading engineer, and the components I am made of represent the best of the nation's material science and craftsmanship.

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: What are your next orders, Ms. Mary-Ann?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: You decide, Mary-Ann. As far as Seymour is concerned, I'm just Ann.

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: Seymour, what would you like to do?

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: My primary directive is to accompany and protect you, Ms. Mary-Ann, on behalf of Alain Guillotin.

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: Oh, you silly— Those were my brother's... Alain's instructions. I'm asking you what you "want" to do.

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: ...I once promised Ms. Mamere that once I found my mistress, I would return to her coordinates and thank her.

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: And that was correct of you. Good dog.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Mary-Ann, do you remember what you once said to me?

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: Yes. Seymour, I hope you can become the "master of your own fate" — that in the future, you will do what you "want" to do, and what you think is right.

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: Ms. Mary-Ann...

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: Do I understand this correctly? Are you saying that my previously-received orders should be regarded as null and void?

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: Yes. So let me ask you again, Seymour — what do you want to do?

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: I wish to remain by your side, Ms. Mary-Ann. But I also wish to accompany Ms. Mamere. However, I calculate that the spatial requirements of those two wishes are incompatible.

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: Perhaps not. We will be taking a trip to explore this world. And Ms. Mamere is an artist, isn't she?

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: Then let our journeys coincide. We will leave our footprints in the deserts, in the forests, and in the snowfields. In the lost Ancient City of Ys, and in Arcadia, and in golden Hyperborea.

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: We will enjoy the sights we see and the stories we write together. What do you think, Seymour?

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: I find that's a very reasonable suggestion, Ms. Mary-Ann. But I will need to ask for Ms. Mamere's consent.

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: Yes, of course. Let us agree to meet here...

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: In any case, I'm eager to meet this artist who's kept you company for so long.

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: Coordinates entered.

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: So, next...

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, and Caterpillar... You were the bravest and strongest of all. Thank you all so much.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Wait, so I'm no longer a knight?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: That story is over. And for me, for "us," you, as you are now, are the realest and most important of all.

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: And not just in the story when you play the role of a knight.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Just like the Holy Blade in the story became a new sword when its mission was complete, so too will the knight return as a new person.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Uh... Paimon can't decide if you're praising or criticizing {NICKNAME} here...

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: It is praise, of course!

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: You have written an end to an unfinishable story, and you have brought us a new tale.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: We will never forget this.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aw, c'mon, there's no need to be so polite!

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: I've also gained a lot from being able to play my role in this tale.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I hope you all have a wonderful trip.

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: Yes! And I am confident we will meet again in the future.

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: Then, it is time for me to return to Ms. Mamere's coordinates.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We can come too! Caterpillar, come with us, would you?

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Very well. I will accompany you.

choices.text: Caterpillar, let's see this through to the end.

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: Thank you for your accurate assessment.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But that's not what Ann was trying to say...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Where would you most like to go right now, Mary-Ann?

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Well... I've remained for far too long in that imaginary past-world.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: The world must have changed a lot after hundreds of years.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: I want to see this world beyond the glass wall. I want to experience new stories.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Are you afraid, Mary-Ann?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I know stories end, but I find it difficult to imagine that everything would end like this. From the moment I was born, the Narzissenkreuz Kingdom was everything to me...

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: I understand that you're feeling more uneasy than I am. You were born for this story. But from now onward, you must start your own story... Ann's story.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: And I must slowly step away from the looming shadow of my past. Neither Lyris's memories nor Mary-Ann Guillotin's represent who I am now.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: We have a long path ahead of us, Ann.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: But I know you'll be alright.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: If you find yourself feeling afraid, we can come back here.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Even if only ruins remain, a seed that drifts here will bloom. So long as we remain, we can always rebuild a new home.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Why are you doing this? Is the truth really that important?

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: What's wrong with forever dwelling on dreams of the past?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It may be that the truth isn't that important.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But the future is.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: Indeed. Even if you all regard me as a villain, I have never once given up on the future.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Wait. You're...!?

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: That is correct. I am Narzissenkr—

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Rene!

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: ...Yes, I am Rene. This is who I am now.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: I am most pleased to see "you both," as well as Ann.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: Your present state could be said to be something beyond human or Oceanid. A state of transcendence.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: As human is to ape, so is superhuman to human. You are now the meaning of Fontaine itself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Is this really a good time to be saying this sorta stuff?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You don't think about anyone else's feelings, do you, Narzissenkreuz?

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: My apologies. I am responsible for the circumstances that led you all here.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: It's okay. I've already forgiven him, Mary-Ann.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Please, look at this.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: This is...!

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: This is the eternity I've always longed to protect...

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Rene.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: Yes?

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: I can't forgive "Narzissenkreuz" just yet. But "Rene"... is a different story.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: The Narzissenkreuz Institute was our home. Why did things turn out this way?

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: It was likely doomed to be thus from the moment Alain had us act out the story of the hero Narzissenkreuz and the evil dragon over and over.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: I, too, miss the way things used to be. But Narzissenkreuz was born out of the delusion of salvation — and what a protracted dream that was.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: But I was roused from that dream. Now, it is your turn.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: It's not a contradiction to accept your past as well as how you'll live your life going forward. That's what Caterpillar told me.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: The apocalypse has been stopped, and the future is full of possibilities.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: The future holds more for you than just pain — this, I promise you.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: If you cannot accept yourself, you could allow Ann to merge with you.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: Then, use the Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz to separate the personas of Lyris and young Mary-Ann.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: That won't be necessary, I'm willing to accept the past. Our little hero Ann's adventure is hers alone.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: I will live on as myself and see what the world you risked everything to save is like, Rene.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? The Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz is...

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: I see. Your will has been conveyed, Mary-Ann. The Holy Blade's purpose has been fulfilled, and its significance in the story has ended.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hmm... Paimon doesn't totally get it, but does it mean that {NICKNAME} won't be able to use that cool title anymore?

response.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
response.text: Let us return to the original topic. You said that you'd like to see the outside. But this is now Guillotin's world. I doubt there will be much to see.

response.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
response.text: However, if you can bring yourself to like it, that would be ideal.

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: Ann, Rene... Shall we travel together?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Absolutely!

response.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
response.text: As for me... Regrettably, you must allow me to decline. There is still something that I must do.

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: Oh, okay... In that case, don't forget to give me your address. I'll write to you about what Ann and I encounter on our journey.

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: Just like when you and Jakob would tell me about what you saw in Sumeru.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Except I'm afraid our journey will have to wait a teeny bit longer. Caterpillar did say that we would have a reunion, or something...

response.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
response.text: That's right. He should be here soon. Let's wait a little longer for him, shall we?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Alright, you two do you. Let's take this opportunity to talk to Mary-Ann, {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME} and Paimon, and—

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Seymour!

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: You knew to come back!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, is it just Paimon, or do you sound a little angry, Mamere?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: #Yes. Even without {NICKNAME} and Paimon's help, my positioning and navigational modules would have allowed me to return.

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Incredible!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, so you were just surprised?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: #Well, I knew you wouldn't disappear with the "token" that symbolizes my life and birth. I also knew that {NICKNAME} and Paimon would be sure to bring you back.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Returning to your side is what I "want" to do. It's not a concept I fully understand, but logic prompts me to do this. I believe this is correct.

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Uh, that's kind of complicated, and I can't say I understand, but never mind. It's... just good that you're back.

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Oh, and this is...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Hello. Don't worry about me. I'm just along for the ride.

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Is that so? Well, you are a fascinating color. And regardless, I'm delighted to see Seymour.

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: #I haven't heard from Father since the message {NICKNAME} passed on. And then Seymour left. It was... difficult for me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Oh, it looks like Mamere doesn't know what happened while you were in a daze...)

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Everyone in Merusea Village helped me during that time. That's what made me realize what Father meant...

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Oh, yes! I've been learning a new style of painting while I was with them!

choices.text: Is it even more novel than before?

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: I think it will be easier to understand! Even the Melusines of Merusea Village can tell what I'm painting now, rather than just saying "Oh, how lovely!"

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow! Paimon can't wait to see your priceless masterpieces!

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Hehe.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, and speaking of paintings, Mary-Ann mentioned something...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Seymour explains the idea of a joint trip.

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Really? That sounds wonderful!

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Let's set off now, then — on our round-the-world trip of artistic creation!

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Yes, let's go. Now. This instant. I'll pack up my art supplies and clothes. You just sit tight and wait for me, alright?

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: Yes, Ms. Mamere.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Woah, you sure are springing into action!

response.speaker: Mamere Inside the House
response.text: Of course. I mean, if you don't act, your dreams will never come true, right?

response.speaker: Mamere Inside the House
response.text: Paints, paints...

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: #While we wait, let me express my gratitude to you, {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, Ms. Paimon, and Mr. Caterpillar.

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: This is based on my own judgment and what, as Ms. Mary-Ann says, I "want" to do. With your help, I have finally been able to complete my task.

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: However, I still do not understand what it means to become "the master of my own fate." Fate, you see, is a concept humans create to help them understand things. It is not real.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa. Paimon doesn't know how to explain this now...

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Didn't they tell you? Just do what you want to do.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: If you always do what you want to do, you'll become the master of your fate.

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: I see. And what I want to do now is to sit here and wait for Ms. Mamere.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay. In that case, Paimon wishes you all a good trip!

response.speaker: Mamere Inside the House
response.text: Thanks, Paimon!

response.speaker: Mamere Inside the House
response.text: Paintings to give them, paintings to give...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Be a good dog and look after Mamere, alright?

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: I will. It is what I want to do.

choices.text: Is it even more... novel than before?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: ...So, the tale of Narzissenkreuz has ended. It is time for me to follow my own path.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Where will you go, Caterpillar?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: That is a good question, Paimon. And since the beginning of time, only the most determined and resilient of people have found their answers.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There you go again!

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I jest, I jest. For now, the only thing I can be sure of is that I still owe Lanoire half a story. But I don't know how it ends yet. I need...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: There's a lot to consider. I don't know where I'll go, but there are a few things I need to find.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is that so...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: #So, goodbye, {NICKNAME}, and farewell, Paimon. Meeting you both has been the most fortunate thing to happen in this "life" of mine.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! Take care, Caterpillar. Don't let anyone find out who you really are! That'd be a pain!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: The hilichurl smiles before turning to leave.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Are you ready to leave?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's wait a little longer.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: There is nothing here now. Just a majestic yet suppressed life force.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: But if you are curious, we can watch some more.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Well, hurry up and get it done, then. We do need to have that get-together, don't we?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: The reason why I'm not worried about everything going smoothly is...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Well, Narzissenkreuz is an absolutely reliable guide, so there won't be any issues with him around.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Narzissenkreuz, where did you come across these things?

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: The Universitas Magistrorum in Khaenri'ah, though they had themselves abandoned those ancient creeds.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: They lost themselves in research into how the power of the "lowest" can combat that of the "highest." They have left the path of wisdom.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: "Io, Io, Pan! That which crosses the billowing waves!"

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, what are you talking about this time?

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: This is a prayer I used to hurl my ego into the sacrificial depths. It comes from an ancient tragedy, though I do not know how it survived until our time.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: The play is called "Ajax," or "Aias." He was the second-strongest warrior in their alliance.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: No one needs saving... and that's great.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Just let me decay here on my own, until everything has broken down, until nothing more than a puddle of dirty water is left...

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Please, stop! I'm begging you! Stay away! This is our Annapausis.

dialogues.speaker: Narzissenkreuz
dialogues.text: You are most talented, Ann. Would you like to inherit Narzissenkreuz's...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I'll pass!

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: You and Caterpillar arrive outside Merusea Village...
